text:
The Devils arrive in Colorado on the second night of a back-to-back, riding four straight wins after a 5-1 rout in Dallas last night that ended the Stars' five-game winning streak. The Avalanche are 2-3-0 in their last five, coming off a 6-2 loss in Nashville three days ago, and they're playing without Zachary L'Heureux. This is a rematch of Oct. 20, when New Jersey won 4-3. Mackenzie Blackwood, projected to start, would play his 300th NHL game.

Our numbers favor the visitors on how the games are played. At five on five, the Devils have taken 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), against 52% for Colorado, and they've won the chance battle in all five of their recent games. Colorado has had more of the chances in only one of its last five. The Avalanche have the better goals-for number, 4.08 a game to 3.42, but they allow 3.25. Our model has it nearly even tonight, 3.0 expected goals to 2.97. The power play leans New Jersey (0.79 expected goals a game to 0.63), as does the penalty kill (0.41 allowed to 0.56). In net, projected starters Jake Allen (-3.06 goals saved above expected this season, 5.39 last year) and Blackwood (-1.04 this season, 8.01 last year) have both been shaky.

Arseny Gritsyuk has scored in five straight games, and as Mike Fink of The Hockey News posted, he added an empty-netter Saturday, "his fifth goal in as many games." We give him a 20% chance to score tonight, though he's due to cool. Jack Hughes is New Jersey's likeliest scorer at 34%. For Colorado, Nathan MacKinnon is at 38% to score and 83% to get a point, and Artturi Lehkonen (31%) has a seven-game point streak.
